assertions.name: symmetric_vs_antisymmetric_guard

description: qou-rutm. The rung asked for a charge lattice for the 5_2 flavour. ANSWER: it is NOT sourceable from the held knots-quivers literature, and the exclusion is STRUCTURAL rather than a failed search. The corpus holds two knots-quivers sources: KRSS (arxiv-1707.02991v1), which works the trefoil only, and Singh et al. (physrevd108106023), which gives explicit symmetric quiver matrices for the double twist family K(p,-m). That family's Alexander polynomial is Delta = 1 - pm*(1-x)^2/x (its eq (5)), so det = |Delta(-1)| = 1+4pm == 1 (mod 4) for every positive p,m. det(5_2) = 7 == 3 (mod 4), so 5_2 is in no member of the family -- SCOPE (b), invariant cited (determinant mod 4), excluding the whole two-parameter family rather than the tabulated members. The formula is confirmed by the paper's own five named (p,m) assignments, all reproduced exactly. GUARD: both sources build SYMMETRIC quivers and eq (98) is ANTISYMMETRIC, so a sourced 5_2 quiver would be the wrong object anyway.

determinant_calibration.method: |det(V + V^T)| with V an exact integer Seifert matrix from spherogram, determinant by Fraction-based elimination
determinant_calibration.why_calibrated_first: the routine is verified against independently known values BEFORE any conclusion rests on it

exclusion.verdict: 5_2 is not K(p,-m) for any positive integers p,m
exclusion.why_b_and_not_a: the argument rules out the entire two-parameter family from an invariant, not the finitely many members that happen to be tabulated
exclusion.consistency_check: the paper's worked twist-knot list is 4_1/6_1/8_1 (dets 5/9/13, all 1 mod 4) and never the odd-index twist knots -- exactly what this predicts

guard_symmetric_vs_antisymmetric.held_sources_build: SYMMETRIC quivers (both say so in their own words)
guard_symmetric_vs_antisymmetric.consequence: a sourced 5_2 quiver would not be eq (98); the two are different objects, not two presentations of one
guard_symmetric_vs_antisymmetric.failure_class: matching an object by shape rather than by structure -- the class that produced the merged 'eq (98) is rank 3' error (a matrix SIZE read as a RANK), corrected in #6643

what_this_does_not_settle.not_claimed: that no 5_2 quiver exists anywhere in the literature
what_this_does_not_settle.measured_scope: the two knots-quivers documents THIS corpus holds
what_this_does_not_settle.disconfirmation: an explicit 5_2 quiver matrix from any source would settle the sourcing question -- but C7 stands regardless, since it would still be symmetric
what_this_does_not_settle.open: whether the A_omega/Route-C programme needs a charge lattice at all once eq (98)'s radical is known to be the mirror-symmetric direction (#6676)
